'''Visual reasoning''' is the process of manipulating one's [[mental image]] of an object in order to reach a certain conclusion – for example, mentally constructing a piece of machinery to experiment with different mechanisms. In a frequently cited paper in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]''<ref>[[Ferguson, Eugene S.]] 1977. The Minds Eye: Non-Verbal Thought in Technology. ''Science'' 197 (4306):827-836.</ref> and a later book,<ref>[[Ferguson, Eugene S.]] 1992. ''Engineering and the mind's eye''. Cambridge, Mass.: MIT Press.</ref> [[Eugene S. Ferguson]], a mechanical engineer and historian of technology, claims that visual reasoning is a widely used tool used in creating technological artefacts. There is ample evidence that visual methods, particularly drawing, play a central role in creating artefacts. Ferguson's visual reasoning also has parallels in philosopher [[David Gooding]]'s<ref>Gooding, David. 1990. ''Experiment and the making of meaning : human agency in scientific observation and experiment''. Dordrecht; Boston: Kluwer Academic Publishers.</ref> argument that experimental scientists work with a combination of action, instruments, objects and procedures as well as words. That is, with a significant non-verbal component.

Ferguson argues that [[Non-Verbal Reasoning|non-verbal reasoning]] does not get much attention in areas like [[history of technology]] and [[philosophy of science]] because the people involved are verbal rather than [[Visual thinking|visual thinkers]].

Those who use visual reasoning, notably architects, designers, engineers, and certain mathematicians conceive and manipulate objects in "the mind's eye" before putting them on paper. Having done this the paper or computer versions (in [[Computer-aided design|CAD]]) can be manipulated by [[metaphor]]ically "building" the object on paper (or computer) before building it physically.

[[Nicola Tesla|Nikola Tesla]] claimed that the first [[alternating current motor]] he built ran perfectly because he had visualized and "run" models of it in his mind before building the [[prototype]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Tesla |first=Nikola |year=2007 |orig-year=first published 1919 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qcAoK07arLYC&pg=PA19 |title=My Inventions: The Autobiography of Nikola Tesla |publisher=Wilder Publications |page=19 |isbn=978-1934451779}}</ref>
